# Smoke test: give me one sentence about reliable

**The short version:** Smoke test: give me one works best as a narrow, instrumented workflow with a visible quality bar. Everything else is optimisation.

## What matters most
- **Define the outcome first.** “Save time” is not measurable. “Cut the weekly report from 3 hours to 30 minutes” is.
- **Design the review step.** Generation is cheap; judgement is the constraint. Put a named owner on every external output.
- **Instrument before you scale.** Capture cycle time and error rate at day one, or you’ll be arguing from anecdotes by week six.
- **Keep the feedback loop short.** The faster a bad output is caught, the cheaper the system is to run.

## A practical sequence
1. **Week 1 — Baseline.** Measure the current workflow end to end, including waiting time.
2. **Week 2 — Prototype.** Build the smallest version that produces a real deliverable.
3. **Week 3 — Pilot.** Run it with 3–5 people who will tell you the truth.
4. **Week 4 — Harden.** Fix the top two failure modes; write the checklist.
5. **Week 5+ — Expand.** Add one adjacent workflow, not five.

## What to watch
| Risk | Early signal | Response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Silent quality drop | Review edits increase | Tighten the prompt and checklist |
| Low adoption | Usage concentrated in one person | Remove a step; don’t add training |
| Cost creep | Credits rising faster than output | Route simple tasks to a cheaper model |

## Bottom line
Treat Smoke test: give me one as an operating change. The teams that win are the ones that redesign review and ownership alongside the tooling.
Build a Q4 launch campaign for our new AI analytics product. Audience: ops leaders at 50–500 person SaaS companies. Budget: $40k.

## Campaign: “See the signal, skip the noise”

**Positioning.** The only analytics layer that turns product + revenue data into a weekly operating brief for ops leaders.

### Channel mix
| Channel | Share | Play |
| --- | --- | --- |
| LinkedIn ABM | 35% | 120 target accounts, 3-touch sequence from founder |
| Partner webinar | 25% | Co-host with a RevOps community; live teardown of a real dashboard |
| Content/SEO | 20% | “Ops brief” template + 4 benchmark posts |
| Paid retargeting | 20% | Demo-request retargeting on pricing + docs visitors |

### 6-week timeline
1. **Week 1–2** — ICP list, narrative testing, landing page.
2. **Week 3** — Webinar + founder LinkedIn series.
3. **Week 4–5** — ABM sequences, case study, retargeting.
4. **Week 6** — Demo sprint and launch recap.

**Success metrics:** 45 qualified demos, $310k pipeline, 3.2% ABM reply rate.

Want me to turn this into the actual LinkedIn copy and webinar outline?

Explain this pandas churn analysis and suggest what to check next:

df.groupby("plan").agg(churn=("churned","mean"), users=("id","nunique"))

This groups customers by plan and computes the churn **rate** alongside cohort size.

### What it tells you
- `churn=("churned","mean")` treats the 0/1 flag as a rate.
- `users=("id","nunique")` protects against duplicate rows.

### Check next
1. **Weight by revenue**, not just users — a small enterprise cohort can dominate ARR impact.
2. **Time-bound it** — use a 90-day window so older cohorts don’t skew the average.
3. **Segment by tenure** — churn is usually front-loaded in month 1–2.

```python
window = df[df["signup_at"] >= "2025-01-01"]
window.groupby(["plan", pd.cut(window.tenure_days, [0,30,90,180,365,9999])]).agg(
    churn=("churned","mean"), users=("id","nunique"), mrr=("mrr","sum")
)
```

> Rule of thumb: any churn rate computed on fewer than 30 accounts should be shown as a range, not a single number.
Draft a concise monthly investor update. Highlights: ARR $1.84M (+11% MoM), net retention 118%, 9 new logos, one enterprise churn. Lowlights: sales cycle up from 31 to 42 days.

**Subject: Northstar — September update ($1.84M ARR, +11% MoM)**

Hi all,

**Highlights**
- ARR reached **$1.84M**, up 11% month over month.
- Net revenue retention held at **118%**.
- Closed **9 new logos**, including 3 in the mid-market.

**Lowlights**
- Average sales cycle extended from **31 → 42 days** as we move upmarket.
- One enterprise account churned after an internal reorg (2.1% of ARR).

**Asks**
- Intros to RevOps leaders at 200–1,000 person SaaS companies.
- Candidate referrals for a senior AE with enterprise experience.

Thanks for the support — reply anytime with questions.

Alex
Compare Orbit and NexAI for mid-market ops teams. Focus on positioning, pricing and AI depth.

## Orbit vs NexAI — mid-market ops

| Dimension | Orbit | NexAI |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Positioning | “Dashboarding for ops” | “AI operating system for teams” |
| Entry price | $49/user | $79/workspace (10 seats) |
| AI depth | Bolt-on summaries | Native agents + tool routing |
| Time to value | 2–3 weeks of setup | Same-day with templates |

**Where Orbit wins:** polished chart library and a mature connector catalog.

**Where NexAI wins:** agents that act on the data, not just visualise it; predictable workspace pricing.

**Recommended wedge:** “Your dashboard can’t write the board update. NexAI can.” — target teams already paying for Orbit but exporting to slides.
Write a 4-email onboarding sequence for new NexAI Business trials. Goal: first agent created within 7 days.

### Email 1 — Welcome (Day 0)
**Subject:** Your first NexAI agent is 4 minutes away
Show the one-screen agent builder. Single CTA: “Build an agent”.

### Email 2 — Quick win (Day 1)
**Subject:** The report that used to take 3 hours
Share a 90-second screen recording of a research agent producing a competitor brief.

### Email 3 — Social proof (Day 3)
**Subject:** How Lumen Labs cut reporting time 62%
One metric, one quote, one CTA to a template.

### Email 4 — Nudge (Day 6)
**Subject:** Want us to build it with you?
Offer a 20-minute working session. Mention the trial end date and what carries over.

scenes.voiceover: Every week, hours disappear into busywork.

scenes.voiceover: Then everything moves at the speed of intent.

scenes.title: Proof
scenes.description: Real workflow, real output. Let the interface do the talking.
scenes.voiceover: One brief. Every source. Ready to send.

scenes.title: Scale
scenes.description: Show the team using it together — asynchronous, calm, in control.
